name: WAM
title: Watermark Anything with Localized Messages
venue: ICLR 2025; inspected arXiv v2 is the evidence version.
sections: Method §§3–4, Eqs. 1–2; evaluation §§5.1–5.3; Appendix G.1–G.3, Table 9; pinned README, params.json, embed/detect and metrics.py.
mechanism: A message-conditioned autoencoder writes a residual; a ViT-based extractor predicts one mask logit and 32 message logits per pixel. Full-image single-message embedding is the relevant post-hoc use. Localization and several messages are additional capabilities, not owner authentication.
native: Native released MIT SA-1B model: 32 raw bits, processing size 256, scaling_w=2.0, scaling_i=1.0 and JND jnd_1_3_blue. RGB input at 512 is ImageNet-normalized; internal bilinear resizing and antialiased residual upsampling preserve the original image. The paper trains on COCO with alpha=.3 and high-resolution JND scaling; those weights differ from this release. Pixel mask uses sigmoid >.5; paper image presence is mask-positive area >.07, calibrated on COCO to about 2.6e-4 FPR. Released README passes RAW message logits to semihard aggregation: select mask >.5, average logits, then compare the average >.5. This differs from averaging probabilities in paper Equation 2; retain the released behavior. An empty mask is an abstention. Official save_image multiplies by 255, adds .5, clamps and converts to uint8. Common known-message presence uses at least 27/32 matches (analytic fair-query tail 5.6537101045e-5); this is a separate endpoint and must not be conjoined with the native image detector. COCO calibration does not automatically transfer to SA-1B weights.
release: Official facebookresearch/watermark-anything@2c08af04d037d5667c02f6ddebbda9ff04581c3e; MIT code and chosen SA-1B checkpoint. https://dl.fbaipublicfiles.com/watermark_anything/wam_mit.pth is 377825938 bytes; inherited metadata SHA256 90ef232384e023bd63245eb0c131abd69d2afc7b8f17a71ccedceb542bf009e2. Source archive SHA256 7baaa18c6774d1397207b262cd077f588150e846fada9c7c7b5ce7d0239ef0b6. No new binary download. COCO-weight licensing is distinct and those weights are not substituted.
regeneration: Primary Table 9, Appendix G.3: DiffPure attack PSNR 30.1/28.4/27.0/24.9 dB corresponds to bit accuracy 100/99.4/71.3/49.1%; VAE attack PSNR 32.9/32.4/28.6/25.5 corresponds to 100/99.8/98.6/53.7%. These are bit accuracies, not TPR at our threshold. The appendix does not specify enough to reproduce model revision, diffusion strength/noise schedule, sampler, prompt, exact evaluation count or every attack resolution; do not infer them from the main 10,000-image COCO/DIV2K evaluation. These curves use COCO weights. VINE and SpreadMark comparisons use different payload, quality and attack conditions; they do not establish this release's R1 outcome.
cost: The paper reports approximately 1.1M embedder and 96M extractor parameters. Checkpoint size is storage, not peak VRAM. Inference needs an embedder and a ViT forward; target-server time and memory remain unmeasured. The core cost remains within the parent budget; this is not a new timing claim.
implication: Maintain separate native mask-presence, common queried-message presence, exact recovery and clean quality columns. Do not silently fix the paper/code threshold discrepancy. Preserve native quality; no outcome-based residual scaling.
ranking: Core: already user-approved; no new arm.
authors: ['Tom Sander', 'Pierre Fernandez', 'Alain Durmus', 'Teddy Furon', 'Matthijs Douze']

name: VINE
title: Robust Watermarking Using Generative Priors Against Image Editing: From Benchmarking to Advances
venue: ICLR 2025; official repository and paper version inspected.
sections: Method §§3.1–3.3; evaluation §§4.1–4.3, Table 1; Appendix C/G.2/H, Table 7; native encoder/decoder and stochastic/deterministic regeneration scripts at the pinned commit.
mechanism: Low-frequency surrogate corruption trains a one-step generative-prior residual encoder and ConvNeXt-B message decoder. VINE-R is the chosen robust post-hoc checkpoint. VINE-Base is a separate quality/robustness point, not an interchangeable baseline.
native: VINE-R uses 100 raw bits. The native encoder takes RGB 256 in [-1,1]; the decoder takes RGB 256 in [0,1], with sigmoid outputs and NumPy rounding. Input uses PIL bicubic resizing; the encoder uses the posterior mode. Its tensor bicubic residual is upsampled onto the original 512-pixel image, clamped, converted through native ToPILImage truncation, saved and reopened as PNG. No ImageNet normalization is used. The text CLI writes 96 text bits plus four zeros; arbitrary 100-bit API use is distinct. Paper/README says SDXL-Turbo, but the constructor loads stabilityai/sd-turbo. Native evaluation reports ROC TPR at FPR below .001 or .01; no universal numerical message-match threshold is published. Common presence at 69/100 matches is a separate fair-query tail rule (9.1571612441e-5), not native TPR at .1% FPR. C0 and wrong-owner behavior must remain visible without outcome-based recalibration.
release: Shilin-LU/VINE@d72f11a93f8de9bc45ef61202b9c8dda2a70cc77. Repository NTUITIVE noncommercial license; HF cards separately say MIT; sd-turbo dependency has Stability AI Community License. Do not label the stack MIT. Encoder Shilin-LU/VINE-R-Enc@0c255688e032e4318c700c485c0625367b70908c: 4019166704 bytes, LFS SHA256 16bf5f2acf5f7d5f00570431f5dc9dd61a8e95f828a2f68483ffe06448293dd6. Decoder VINE-R-Dec@0f094b300be71a358f7c1769221f50318f1b4d74: 354802864 bytes, SHA256 9aded1fc22efe47bdafc8f436f81953cd06bde1d6c7242f86bf101c020d7eea0. sd-turbo@b261bac6fd2cf515557d5d0707481eafa0485ec2; combined needed fp32 stack 9533935644 bytes. Immutable URLs are in retained manifest.json. No weights downloaded.
regeneration: Table 1 gives VINE-R PSNR 37.34, SSIM .9934, LPIPS .0063 and stochastic/deterministic regeneration TPR 99.66/99.98% at .1% FPR, averaged over severities. VINE-Base gives 40.51/.9954/.0029 and 91.03/99.25%. Official stochastic code loads stabilityai/stable-diffusion-2-1, fp16 revision fp16, DDIM, noise indices 60 through 240 in increments of 20, requested 50 inference steps and head-start logic 50-max(noise//20,1), CFG 7.5, empty prompt unless captions are supplied, and sampled latent posterior. Deterministic code uses SD2.1-base fp32, DPM multistep inverse/forward scheduler of order 2, 15/25/35/45 steps, CFG 1, empty prompt/negative prompt and posterior mean times .18215. The native benchmark uses 512 pixels. COUNT CONFLICT: Table 1 caption says 5,000 images per editing method; Section 4.2 says 1,000 stochastic and 1,000 deterministic sources; Section 4.3 describes m times 1,000 over severities. Preserve all statements without claiming 5,000 independent sources. Quality uses 10,000 UltraEdit images. Native ROC calibration is empirical against unmarked images; no 1e-4 calibration is claimed.
cost: Table 7 reports .0795 seconds and 4,982 MB on NVIDIA Quadro RTX6000, averaged over 1,000 images. The phase/batch scope is insufficiently explicit to derive whole-grid time. Approximately 9.53 GB of required fp32 weight storage is not peak VRAM. Target-server timing remains unmeasured.
implication: Independent SDXL regeneration is absent from these SD2.1 attack scripts. The generative prior's name does not prove independent-encoder transfer. Freeze actual released sd-turbo and preprocessing, and label both operating points.
ranking: Core: user-approved VINE-R; VINE-Base remains excluded.
authors: ['Shilin Lu', 'Zihan Zhou', 'Jiayou Lu', 'Yuanzhi Zhu', 'Adams Wai-Kin Kong']

name: TrustMark
title: TrustMark: Universal Watermarking for Arbitrary Resolution Images
venue: Final ICCV 2025 paper, pp. 18629–18639, also inspected. Its exact title is TrustMark: Robust Watermarking and Watermark Removal for Arbitrary Resolution Images. The final version takes precedence where stated.
sections: arXiv v1 §§3.1–3.3,4.1–4.4; final ICCV PDF pp. 3–7 (method, Algorithm 1, experimental setup, Table 3); Table 3 visually verified from rendered page 7; pinned official Q loader/config/LICENSE.
mechanism: The image encoder uses MUNIT components, additional 1×1 layers and spectral/quality losses; a ResNet50 sigmoid decoder recovers the message. ReMark is a separate learned removal and re-watermarking module. A recovered public identifier is a provenance pointer, not owner authentication.
native: The paper network resolution is 256. The pinned Python Q release resizes the encoder input to 256×256 and the decoder input to 245×245 using PIL bilinear (trustmark.py:119–122,451–458). It normalizes to [-1,1], interpolates the encoder residual onto the original image, uses lambda=1 by default, and clamps. Native Q with use_ECC=True and BCH_5 carries 61 payload bits, 35 BCH parity bits and 4 header bits. With use_ECC=False, the release sets detected=True unconditionally; this is not a presence detector. P1 must preserve the native BCH configuration and report native detected/schema, recovery of the expected 61-bit payload, and raw 100-bit agreement descriptively. A further common-query cutoff needs a null model for structured codewords and headers; Binomial(100,.5) cannot simply be assumed. Neither BCH success nor an analytic payload rule establishes empirical image FPR. The final paper's alpha_max=27.5 quality setting and alpha_max=20 removal setting differ.
release: adobe/trustmark@6df5a0a29b51cbec832695fdf02051a1937e37bd. Final paper footnote and official LICENSE explicitly release code/models under MIT. Q encoder/decoder at https://cai-watermark.adobe.net/watermarking/trustmark-models/encoder_Q.ckpt and decoder_Q.ckpt; official loader MD5 values 700328b8754db934b2f6cb5e5185d81f and 4ced90e9cfe13e3295ad082887fe9187. These are integrity metadata, not a new SHA256 or immutable release revision; weight SHA256 remains unresolved without downloading.
regeneration: Final ICCV Table 3 uses alpha_max=20 and lambda=1: no removal gives PSNR 40.20 and bit accuracy .970; Zhao et al. denoising with sigma=.3 gives PSNR 9.23 and bit accuracy .660. Table 3 was visually checked on rendered page 7. Section 4.1 states DIV2K training and validation splits, without an explicit numeric count; a distinct Table 3 count is not stated. Exact denoiser revision, sampler, steps and prompt are unspecified. VINE Table 1's third-party raw-100-bit variant instead gives stochastic/deterministic TPR 9.22/34.20% at .1% FPR and quality 41.27/.9910/.0026, under the VINE card's attack conditions and count conflict. WAM Appendix G.3 uses a different 40-bit configuration: DiffPure bit accuracy 100/98.3/74.9/54.3% and VAE 100/100/99.9/98.1%. These are different attacks and operating points, not necessarily contradictory results.
cost: Final ICCV Section 4.1 reports encoding 125 ms and decoding 25 ms on RTX3090; the stated 48-hour training time is not inference. VINE Table 7 reports .0705 seconds and 648 MB on Quadro RTX6000, averaged over 1,000 images. Hardware and timing scopes differ; neither is a measurement on the future rented server.
implication: P1 remains the first additional baseline proposal because the official Q release is practical and independently published. Its native ECC payload, 245-pixel decoder resize and quality must stay visible. Final ICCV paper access is now closed through PDF rendering/OCR and visual checking of Table 3.
ranking: P1 TrustMark Q retained; proposed, excluded from core.
authors: ['Tu Bui', 'Shruti Agarwal', 'John Collomosse']

name: StegaStamp
title: StegaStamp: Invisible Hyperlinks in Physical Photographs
sections: §§4.1–4.4 encoder/decoder/BCH and print-camera pipeline; §§5.1–5.5 and Table 2; official README/LICENSE.
mechanism: A U-Net residual encoder and spatial-transformer CNN decoder learn robustness to the print-camera channel. Photograph localization may use a separate segmentation model; it is not a calibrated arbitrary-image watermark detector.
native: Native images are 400×400 with 100 physical bits. The public text encoder accepts at most 7 bytes (56 useful bits), adds BCH parity and padding; arbitrary 100-bit research payloads are a distinct operating point. Preserve RGB conversion, resizing and native TensorFlow quantization if proposed. No universal numerical image-presence threshold is published. The detector needs an expected message for queried-message presence; BCH decoding alone is a different endpoint.
release: tancik/StegaStamp@c984446048b826587ca1875027b0a1dc1885fb30, MIT code. README references saved_models/stegastamp_pretrained; exact stable checkpoint artifact/hash not verified. TensorFlow 1.13-era execution dependency; no install attempted and no port is counted as faithful release.
regeneration: The original paper evaluates physical print-camera corruption: 1,890 photographs from 105 samples across 18 conditions, mean bit accuracy 98.7%. Its 500-image quality evaluation reports PSNR 28.50, SSIM .905 and LPIPS .101 for 100 bits. VINE Table 1 instead reports stochastic/deterministic regeneration TPR 91.09/92.13% at .1% FPR, with quality 29.65/.9107/.0645; use the VINE card's 512-pixel preprocessing, attack scripts and unresolved count conflict. ZoDiac Table 15 uses 96 bits and threshold 61/96, with observed FPR .056: at 40/60/80/100/120/140/160/180/200 denoising steps, WDR is .588/.286/.098/.032/.010/.002/.002/0/0. That is neither native 100-bit+BCH nor equal-FPR evidence. Exact attack model revision, sampler and prompt are not fully specified there.
cost: VINE Table 7 reports .0672 seconds and 1,984 MB on Quadro RTX6000, averaging 1,000 images. Target-server timing and peak VRAM remain unmeasured; legacy TensorFlow compatibility creates engineering uncertainty.
implication: P2 remains a recognizable historical comparator, but its native quality is below the thesis's strict clean gate. Keep its quality failure visible instead of rescaling it after seeing outcomes. It is a proposal only.
ranking: P2 retained, deferred until artifact and faithful runtime preflight; excluded.
authors: ['Matthew Tancik', 'Ben Mildenhall', 'Ren Ng']

name: InvisMark
title: InvisMark: Invisible and Robust Watermarking for AI-generated Image Provenance
sections: §§2.1–2.4; §§3.1–3.5, Tables 2–3, Figure 4 and UUID extension.
mechanism: A learned high-resolution residual encoder and ConvNeXt decoder optimize visual quality and distortion robustness. The training set includes 100,000 privately generated DALL-E 3 images.
native: The main paper uses 100-bit messages. Its separate 256-bit BCH extension carries a 128-bit UUID; these are different capacities and operating points. High-resolution evaluation is established, but the inspected paper text does not establish the exact released encoder input size. Native clamp, interpolation, serialization and an image-presence threshold need release verification. Pixel Seal reports six fixed bits in the 100-bit implementation, implying only 94 varying bits in that comparison; this is a third-party observation, not a newly measured result.
release: microsoft/InvisMark@8d5ce55705ada1c2daf642c97f7ff3ae6dbd1825, MIT repository. Official README OneDrive checkpoint folder available as a pointer; immutable revision/hash and durable direct artifact access not verified. Private 100k DALL-E 3 training images unavailable; do not replace weights with retraining and call it native.
regeneration: Section 3.3/Figure 4 evaluates SD2.1 regeneration at noise settings 1, 3, 5, 10, 20, 60 and 100 on 10 images. Bit accuracy approaches chance near attacked PSNR 25 dB. Per-setting bit accuracy is graphical and was not digitized; no exact scalar is invented. Sampler, prompts, seed replication and exact count per condition are incompletely reported. Table 2 reports clean PSNR 51.4 and SSIM .998 on 900 DIV2K and 900 DALL-E 3 images. High clean quality does not establish regeneration detection.
cost: A released feed-forward encoder/decoder would avoid per-image optimization. No adequately conditioned target inference time or peak memory was established; any future estimate must include the high-resolution residual path and actual checkpoint.
implication: A useful high-quality comparator for later work, but checkpoint provenance, fixed-bit structure and regeneration weakness prevent treating it as a turnkey replacement for a core arm.
authors: ['Rui Xu', 'Mengya Hu', 'Deren Lei', 'Yaxi Li', 'David Lowe', 'Alex Gorevski', 'Mingyu Wang', 'Emily Ching', 'Alex Deng']

name: RoSteALS
title: RoSteALS: Robust Steganography using Autoencoder Latent Space
sections: §§3.1–3.2;§§4.1–4.3 and evaluation definitions; official README/license/checkpoint metadata.
mechanism: A frozen pretrained VQ image autoencoder receives a learned secret-conditioned residual in its latent representation; a ResNet extractor recovers the payload from the decoded image. Existing images can be encoded and marked, so this qualifies as post-hoc.
native: The reported setting uses 100 bits at 256×256 with a VQ-f4 codec and approximately 300,000 trainable secret-encoder parameters. The decoder is image-only, with an expected message needed for query scoring. The paper's word-accuracy definition allows fewer than 20% bit errors; it is not exact payload recovery. No calibrated universal presence threshold is provided. Release preprocessing and rounding require later adapter verification.
release: TuBui/RoSteALS@8c09b022a362ffdf977a86f355e5af339793d9c9, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0. Official 520 MB watermark checkpoint https://kahlan.cvssp.org/data/Flickr25K/tubui/cvpr23_wmf/epoch=000017-step=000449999.ckpt; frozen VQ dependency https://ommer-lab.com/files/latent-diffusion/vq-f4.zip. Neither downloaded; immutable hash and dependency license/version remain unresolved.
regeneration: The original evaluation covers conventional distortions and ImageNet-C, not a fully conditioned diffusion-regeneration experiment. It therefore provides no defensible model/strength/sampler/prompt/count/TPR tuple for R1. The method and evaluation are V2-inspected even though regeneration evidence is absent.
cost: Training with batch size 4 is reported to fit a 12 GB GPU. This is not measured inference memory. Inference needs the frozen VQ codec plus secret encoder and extractor; checkpoint size is storage, not peak VRAM.
implication: The explicit latent post-hoc pathway matters for the taxonomy, but the older codec and missing direct regeneration result make it lower priority than P1/P9.
authors: ['Tu Bui', 'Shruti Agarwal', 'Ning Yu', 'John Collomosse']

name: ZoDiac
title: Attack-Resilient Image Watermarking Using Stable Diffusion
venue: NeurIPS 2024 main track; official proceedings verified; numerical evidence is inspected arXiv v2.
sections: §§3.2–3.3,4.1; Appendix B.6/Table 15,B.7/Table 16 and Appendix D timing/memory.
mechanism: Per-image optimization writes a Fourier-ring watermark into an image's diffusion latent using DDIM inversion and a structural-similarity constraint. Verification requires diffusion inversion and a keyed ring test; this is a zero-bit post-hoc method.
native: The default uses SD2.1-base at 512×512, ring radius 10 in the last latent channel, 100 Adam iterations, 50 denoising steps and target SSIM .92. The stated default detection condition is 1-p>.9. It is not a multi-bit payload, and the expected ring/key and generator are detector side information. The published thresholds have percent-level measured FPR, far above the study's analytic common-query target.
release: zhanglijun95/ZoDiac@89f864d2e4f6f33663dc69b4d99bee49073e194c. Code inspected; no repository license verified (public accessibility is not a license). Requires SD2.1-base; weight/dependency permissions and full reproducible pin not resolved for a proposed run. No checkpoint download or inference performed.
regeneration: The evaluation uses 500 images from each of MS-COCO, DiffusionDB and WikiArt. Default learned-compression attacks use bmshj/cheng quality 3; Zhao23 regeneration uses 60 steps. Appendix Table 15's COCO strength study reports, at p*=.95 and observed FPR .032, WDR .980/.974/.950/.940/.924/.912/.894/.866/.818 for 40/60/80/100/120/140/160/180/200 steps. At p*=.90 and FPR .062, the corresponding values are .988/.988/.964/.970/.952/.946/.938/.926/.898. Attack PSNR falls from 27.15 to 22.44. The prose says .998 to .898 whereas the first table entry is .988; preserve the discrepancy. Exact attack revision, sampler and prompt are incompletely specified.
cost: Appendix D reports RTX8000 fp32 peak memory 15,552 MiB and model storage 5,308 MiB. Embedding is 255.94/159.47/65.35/45.41 seconds with 50/30/10/1 steps. Table 16 gives quality 29.41/.92/.09. These reported costs and quality differ substantially from a feed-forward high-quality baseline.
implication: Useful counterevidence to sweeping removal claims, but its detector cost, side information, image quality and high FPR preclude a fair substitution into the cheap core.
authors: ['Lijun Zhang', 'Xiao Liu', 'Antoni Viros Martin', 'Cindy Xiong Bearfield', 'Yuriy Brun', 'Hui Guan']

name: PhaseMark
title: PhaseMark: A Post-hoc, Optimization-Free Watermarking of AI-generated Images in the Latent Frequency Domain
sections: §§2.1–2.3,3.1–3.3, Tables 1–2; official code README/LICENSE.
mechanism: A training-free SD2.1 VAE latent watermark modifies phases in a central Fourier annulus. Antipodal phase modulation, phase-constrained quantization, iterative phase synchronization and spatial phase synchronization are separately evaluated variants.
native: The method uses 32 bits per latent channel (128 total) in a 44×44 latent region, annulus radii 10–18, 2×2 Hermitian groups and APM phases ±pi/2. SPS uses gamma=.8. The paper's detection threshold uses a binomial alpha=.01; identification at N=10^6 applies a Bonferroni adjustment. Wording that matches 'exceed' the threshold and an inclusive binomial tail must be reconciled before any adapter. The VAE and expected message are side information. Native quantization/preprocessing must come from the pinned source.
release: thomas11809/PhaseMark@dfe42ad0449459e26fe1579957c6d05ccdee9b92 is the verified official repository, licensed CC BY-NC 4.0. There are no learned watermark weights, but an SD2.1 VAE dependency remains necessary. The README uses a Manojb mirror; the immutable dependency pin and licensing still need resolution.
regeneration: Tables 1–2 use 1,000 SD2.1-generated 512-pixel images. APM TPR at 1% FPR is .996 for VAE-B, .997 for VAE-C and 1.000 for Diff. Attack definitions use bmshj/cheng quality 3 and Zhao23 diffusion regeneration at 60 steps. DDIM 50 and CFG 7.5 describe source generation, not necessarily the attack sampler. Exact attack revision, prompt and empirical negative calibration are incomplete. PCQ quality is PSNR 34.156 versus a VAE reconstruction ceiling of 36.4193; no 1e-4 detection result is established.
cost: Table 2 reports .142 seconds embedding and .050 seconds decoding; hardware/phase scope is not sufficiently established for a target-server claim. Full VAE roundtrips and actual peak memory must be included in future timing.
implication: P3 is retained as a proposal because the mechanism differs from learned pixel residuals. Its native quality and alpha=.01 endpoint are materially unequal to the thesis gate; do not tune them on development outcomes to manufacture comparability.
ranking: P3 preserved; proposed/deferred behind P1 and P9; excluded.
authors: ['Sung Ju Lee', 'Nam Ik Cho']

name: MBRS
title: MBRS : Enhancing Robustness of DNN-based Watermarking by Mini-Batch of Real and Simulated JPEG Compression
sections: §§3.1–3.3,4.1–4.2; official README, repository tree and release metadata.
mechanism: A neural image encoder and decoder train with mini-batches containing real JPEG, simulated JPEG and identity corruption, allowing gradients to flow on only the differentiable branches.
native: The original paper studies 64 bits at 128×128 and 625 bits at 400×400. Official released configurations include 30 bits at 128 and 256 bits at 256; these cannot be treated as one interchangeable payload. No universal image-presence cutoff is published. Exact clamp, serialization and normalization must be tied to the selected release.
release: jzyustc/MBRS@2bab0df66480f66cfdef534d38c851354ee2c6aa. Official code and Google Drive weights folder https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1A_SAqvU2vMsHxki0s9m9rKa-g8B6aghe?usp=sharing. No LICENSE file in inspected tree/API license null; license unverified, not MIT by assumption. Checkpoint hashes/immutable revisions unresolved.
regeneration: Original training uses 10,000 ImageNet images and evaluation 5,000 COCO images. The paper reports BER below .01% at JPEG quality 50 with PSNR above 36 dB, but no original diffusion-regeneration evaluation. VINE's 30-bit MBRS baseline has quality 27.37/.8940/.1877 and stochastic/deterministic TPR 99.53/99.35% at .1% FPR. That result uses VINE's attack scripts and unresolved source-count statements, not the original paper's native quality or a matched SDXL test.
cost: VINE Table 7 reports .0053 seconds and 938 MB on Quadro RTX6000, mean over 1,000 images. This is a third-party configuration and hardware measurement, not a local estimate.
implication: A strong illustration of quality/robustness confounding: its high regeneration TPR in VINE comes with very low clean quality. Missing license evidence also blocks a ready-to-run proposal.
authors: ['Zhaoyang Jia', 'Han Fang', 'Weiming Zhang']

name: SSL
title: Watermarking Images in Self-Supervised Latent Spaces
sections: §§3.1–3.4,4.1–4.3; official README/LICENSE and DINO/normalization asset listing.
mechanism: Image optimization moves a frozen self-supervised feature representation into a secret detection cone or toward keyed bit carriers. Whitening statistics and the chosen DINO network are detector dependencies.
native: The zero-bit cone test has a theoretical target FPR of 10^-6 under its feature-distribution model. The distinct multi-bit experiment uses 30 carriers in a 2,048-dimensional feature space. Reported optimization uses 100 Adam iterations, learning rate .01 and a PSNR constraint. The code distinguishes YFCC and COCO whitening; substituting statistics changes the detector.
release: facebookresearch/ssl_watermarking@3e65334bd28ecbc66756f0179def9dc4c88a6acc, CC BY-NC 4.0 (actual LICENSE inspected). Official dino_r50_plus.pth and out2048_yfcc_orig.pth under https://dl.fbaipublicfiles.com/ssl_watermarking/; README distinguishes resized YFCC and COCO whitening. Immutable weight hashes unresolved; no download.
regeneration: The original paper reports zero false detections on 100,000 YFCC images and one on 1,281,167 ImageNet images for the zero-bit setting, but no matched diffusion-regeneration tuple. VINE's 30-bit comparison reports quality 41.77/.9796/.0351 and stochastic/deterministic TPR .76/9.70% at .1% FPR. Those are different endpoints and use VINE's attack/count conditions.
cost: VINE Table 7 reports 2.1938 seconds and 1,072 MB on Quadro RTX6000 for a 1,000-image mean. Per-image optimization makes this slower than the feed-forward comparators; no target-server timing exists.
implication: Keep analytic feature-cone FPR, empirical image FPR and queried-message recovery separate. Its detector side information and optimization cost make it a literature control, not a new core arm.
authors: ['Pierre Fernandez', 'Alexandre Sablayrolles', 'Teddy Furon', 'Hervé Jégou', 'Matthijs Douze']

name: SimuFreeMark
title: SimuFreeMark: A Noise-Simulation-Free Robust Watermarking Against Image Editing
mechanism: A low-frequency latent watermark combines a frozen diffusion VAE with a learned residual encoder. A central FFT low-pass surrogate and restored high-frequency content avoid running iterative diffusion in training.
native: The reported setting is 512-pixel RGB, 64 raw bits, a central 20% FFT region, latent residual alpha=.2 and pixel range [-.5,.5]. CNN sigmoid outputs are rounded to bits. No native calibrated presence threshold or ECC is specified; executable resizing, clamping and quantization could not be verified because no official release was found.
release: Exact-title web and GitHub repository searches found no verified official code or weights. No released implementation or checkpoint license was established; faithful implementation would be new work.
regeneration: Training uses 20,000 COCO images; testing uses 1,000 UltraEdit images with instructions and masks. Table 2 reports SDIP+ full-image inpainting/regeneration bit accuracy 97.64/94.05/92.25% at strengths .1/.3/.5, and InstructPix2Pix 90.42%. Clean quality is PSNR 39.19 and SSIM .990. Exact model revisions, sampler, steps, prompt strings and per-strength seed counts are incompletely specified. These are bit accuracies without a calibrated negative population, not TPR.
cost: A feed-forward latent encoder would require a VAE roundtrip, but neither target inference time nor peak memory is established. Avoid translating training efficiency into an invented runtime.
implication: Directly relevant evidence for surrogate-trained regeneration robustness, but release and attack-detail gaps prevent a faithful runnable proposal now.
authors: ['Yichao Tang', 'Mingyang Li', 'Di Miao', 'Sheng Li', 'Zhenxing Qian', 'Xinpeng Zhang']

name: SpecGuard
title: SpecGuard: Spectral Projection-based Advanced Invisible Watermarking
sections: §§3.1–3.3 including Eqs. 13–17/Algorithm 1;§§4.1–4.6; Appendix 12.2/Table 9 attack settings.
mechanism: Spectral watermarking learns how to modify wavelet high-frequency components using a compact convolutional network and a learned extraction threshold. It is applied to an existing image.
native: The inspected setting uses radius 100, 32 convolution channels, watermark strength 20 and theta initialized to .001 and learned. Payloads include 48/64/128/256 bits; Table 1 also compares 30-bit variants at 256/512/1024 resolutions. Algorithm 1's learned theta is a bit-extraction threshold, not calibrated image presence. The main 128-bit clean result is PSNR 42.89, SSIM .99 and BRA .99; do not assume identical quality across capacities.

P9 proposes only 60 clean marked images and 180 R1 strength-.2 regenerations, with shared C0 outputs reused. Assuming 8–20 seconds per regeneration and .15 hours for marking/readout gives .55–1.15 hours; planning allowance .55–1.25 hours. This is an explicit workload estimate, not a measurement.
implication: P9 remains the second additional proposal because the native release is modern, permissively licensed and high quality. The original paper has no direct regeneration result; the separate SNW study supplies conditional third-party evidence at a rescaled, whitened operating point. Neither establishes SDXL transfer for P9. It remains excluded from the core.

mechanism: A black-box training approach embeds a key-dependent watermark using jigsaw permutations and a human-aligned variation discriminator to distinguish useful edits from destructive changes.
native: The 4×4 shuffle provides 16! permutations, approximately 44 bits of key entropy, not a recoverable 44-bit payload. This is a zero-bit detector requiring the key. Native TPR at 1% FPR uses ROC calibration; no universal numerical threshold is published. The exact released normalization, quantization and inference resolution are unverified; batch size 256 is not image resolution.

sections: §§3.1–3.5,4.1–4.4, Tables 1/4; official README/LICENSE.
mechanism: A U-Net image encoder and residual decoder are trained with partial instruction-driven denoising sampling guidance through the last diffusion steps, improving robustness to instruction editing.
native: The reported operating point is 512×512 with 64 raw bits. No ECC or native calibrated presence cutoff is specified. InstructPix2Pix uses Euler 20 steps, text CFG 10 and image CFG 1.5. Table 1 reports BER 2.6579% and quality 41.9142/.9910; real-image BER is 2.6062% with quality 41.4038/.9922. name: NAWE
title: NAWE: Digital Watermarking with Neural-Assisted Watermark Extraction
sections: §§3.1–3.3,4.1–4.4, robustness grid and OFAT evaluation.
mechanism: A training-free denoising-residual carrier uses a pretrained denoiser, synchronization and error correction to recover a keyed payload from an existing image.
native: Native 512-pixel encoding uses 48 payload bits plus 16 CRC bits, Polar coding to 256 bits at rate 1/4, and 68 synchronization bits. The reported s2 setting uses GS-DRUNet sigma 18 and PSNR target 40. Key/nonce, synchronization search, RANSAC and CRC are detector-side information. Multiple candidate searches make a naive single-test CRC or binomial FPR unjustified. Exact rounding and serialization remain unverified.
release: Exact web and GitHub searches found no verified official NAWE implementation or weights. Public denoiser dependencies are not a NAWE release. License, immutable pin, preprocessing and artifact hashes remain unknown.
regeneration: The robustness grid uses 100 COCO images; the one-factor-at-a-time evaluation covers 156 arms in 34 families on 100 images. These are conventional geometric/photometric distortions, not diffusion regeneration. OFAT BER .07 is computed on returned messages, whereas WER accounts for all messages; the conditioning matters. There is no direct regeneration model/strength/sampler/prompt/calibrated-TPR tuple.
cost: Training-free does not mean free inference: denoising, synchronization and candidate search are required. No sufficiently conditioned runtime or peak memory was established for the proposed server.
implication: Relevant to synchronization and structured-payload false positives, but absent direct regeneration evidence and release prevent immediate addition.

name: SNW
title: Optimizing and Securing the Modern Watermarking Channel for Images
venue: arXiv September 2026 preprint; no verified final venue.
sections: Sections 2 through 4, 5, 6.1 through 6.2; Appendix C.1, F, G and H.2; Table 6. Method, evaluation and security scope were read, not only the abstract.
mechanism: The authors adapt PixelSeal's U-Net embedder and ConvNeXt extractor to a 768-dimensional continuous unit-vector channel. A keyed semi-orthogonal matrix rotates a codeword into a secret subspace, with an orthogonal Gaussian component. Alignment, isotropy and quality losses train the channel; a separate anti-spoof loss targets residual transfer. It explicitly marks existing images. Continuous messages are allowed by the formulation, but the reported evaluation uses binary codewords.
native: The channel dimension L is 768. Evaluation uses M'=L and alpha=1, so the tested physical codeword has 768 bits. Abstract maximum capacity 656 and table-specific capacities are different quantities. All compared methods are rescaled to 48 dB PSNR, and decoder features are whitened using statistics from one million unmarked MFlickr images. This is a modified operating point and extra calibration side information. The key, codebook and expected codeword support attribution. No universal numerical image-presence cutoff, empirical FPR or implemented practical ECC recovery is established. Reported Shannon capacity is derived from empirical bit accuracy under an independent-bit assumption; it is not recovered useful payload or TPR.
release: No official implementation, checkpoint or corresponding code/model license was established from the inspected paper and exact-name release searches. The arXiv document license is not a code license. A faithful implementation would be new work, not a runnable native release. PixelSeal's official release does not release SNW-specific learned weights or whitening statistics.
regeneration: General evaluation uses 1,000 MFlickr images at 1,024 pixels and COCO training; at 48 dB, reported LPIPS is .0047 for SNW versus .0034 for PixelSeal, .0025 for VideoSeal and .0010 for TrustMark. Appendix H.2/Table 6 instead uses 200 MFlickr images. Its entries are rate/capacity bits, NOT bit accuracy: SNW identity .892/684.7, VAE .495/380.3, Sana 2 steps .479/368.1, 4 steps .388/298.3, 8 steps .145/111.5, 10 steps .068/52.2 and 20 steps .001/.8. PixelSeal gives identity .939/240.5, VAE .555/142.0, Sana 2 .519/132.8, 4 .357/91.3, 8 .076/19.4, 10 .025/6.4 and 20 .003/.8. The text describes a frozen-VAE roundtrip and DiffPure inversion of the last t steps followed by regeneration. Exact checkpoint/VAE, strength, sampler, prompts and seed replication are not established; Sana step labels must not be mapped to our SDXL strengths. These capacity estimates are neither calibrated detections nor a native PixelSeal result. Appendix G's 200-image residual-transfer experiment reports spoofed capacity 86.5 bits for vanilla SNW and .2 for anti-spoof training, versus identity 678/682.2. This is a specific attack, not a general forgery guarantee.
cost: No adequately conditioned end-to-end inference time or peak VRAM was established. The PixelSeal-family backbone plus key transforms and whitening suggests feed-forward inference, but this is an architectural inference, not measured target-server cost. Training cost and parameter storage cannot replace that measurement.
implication: A recent distinct post-hoc method closes a search gap and supplies qualified third-party PixelSeal regeneration evidence. The covariance/PCA security statement is conditional on its statistical model; Section 2.3 explicitly separates adversarial robustness from its security scope. Capacity, whitening and attack settings limit transfer to our study. No extra proposal or core arm is added.
